note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Severe persistent headache for 3 days, began suddenly upon waking.
- Character: Diffuse headache, worse over right supraorbital area; continuous; intensity ~8/10, decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but does not resolve.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting lights”/visual disturbances; mild nausea (no vomiting).
- Negatives: No tingling, numbness, weakness; no changes in smell or taste; no fever reported (temperature not checked); no URI/sinus symptoms; no nosebleeds or hemoptysis.
- Triggers/modifiers: Worse with bright light; brief stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with abrupt head movement; sleep unaffected (not waking from sleep) but present on waking.
- Prior headaches: Occasional brief headaches responsive to ibuprofen; no prior visual symptoms, nausea, or vomiting with headaches.
- Functional impact: Difficulty focusing; reduced ability to work from home; missed part/all of the last two workdays.
- Recent eye exam: “Recent” eye check reported normal.
- Travel: No recent travel abroad.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Prior issues: Unspecified pain in youth with no cause found, resolved.
- Medications:
  - Oral contraceptive pill (specific product not documented); started ~1 year ago; no side effects reported; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Ibuprofen as needed for headache; partial relief; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - New prescription planned: stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Acetaminophen advised concurrently with prescribed NSAID; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Blood pressure: Reported normal at pharmacy ~1 year ago when starting pill.
- Family history: Mother with migraines (with vomiting).
- Social: Lives alone; works from home; nonsmoker; alcohol ~3 drinks once weekly (approximate; transcript unclear). No recreational drug use reported.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination performed during this telehealth visit.
- Planned: Neurological exam and fundoscopic (optic disc) examination at in-person visit; blood pressure measurement.

Impression:
- Acute severe headache x 3 days with photophobia and visual phenomena; likely migraine, but requires in-person evaluation to exclude secondary causes.

Management Plan:
- Medication:
  - Prescribe NSAID stronger than ibuprofen (name not documented); take with food.
  - May take acetaminophen concurrently; avoid additional ibuprofen while on prescribed NSAID (implied substitution).
- Evaluation:
  - Book in-person appointment for full neurological exam and fundoscopy.
  - Check blood pressure at visit; review contraceptive suitability if migraine with visual symptoms is confirmed.
- Safety net:
  - If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes in character before the appointment, go to the emergency department (A&E) for urgent assessment.
  - If symptoms settle before the appointment, cancel as appropriate.
- Education:
  - Discussed possible migraine etiology and potential need to change contraceptive if migraine with visual symptoms is confirmed.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with new-onset severe continuous headache for 3 days, photophobia, and intermittent visual disturbances. No focal neurological symptoms or systemic red flags reported. Likely migraine, but in-person neurologic and ocular examination and BP check are planned. Short-term symptomatic treatment initiated with a stronger NSAID plus acetaminophen.

Key Takeaways:
- Start the prescribed NSAID instead of ibuprofen and you may also take acetaminophen; always take NSAIDs with food.
- Arrange an in-person visit for neurological and eye examination and a blood pressure check.
- Seek urgent care if the headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or changes in character before your appointment.

Next Steps:
- Schedule clinic appointment for neurological exam, fundoscopic exam, and BP measurement.
- Reassess diagnosis after examination; if migraine with visual symptoms is confirmed, review and potentially change oral contraceptive.
- Cancel appointment if symptoms fully resolve.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing elements: No vitals; no neurological or fundoscopic exam findings; exact name and dosing of new NSAID not documented; acetaminophen dosing not documented; specific oral contraceptive name and dose not documented; comprehensive medication reconciliation limited.
- Internal conflicts: None noted beyond minor ambiguity in alcohol intake (“three once a week”).
- Transcript quality: Several inaudible/unclear segments; some patient identifiers and medication names not captured.
